newsitem.title: USA: No suspects yet in Colorado girl's murder.
newsitem.headline: No suspects yet in Colorado girl's murder.

text.p: Two weeks after the murder of 6-year-old beauty pageant winner JonBenet Ramsey police have been unable to identify any suspects, officials said Wednesday.

"They're debriefing officers and going through material," Boulder police spokeswoman Leslie Aaholm said. She would not comment on published reports that part of a draft or "practice" ransom note was found in the home where the child's body was discovered Dec. 26.

The body was found in the basement of the family's 15-room home about eight hours after her mother said she had found a ransom note demanding $118,000 on the back staircase of the Boulder residence. The Rocky Mountain News and The Denver Post reported a second note had been found and one report said it appeared an effort had been made to disguise the handwriting.
"But as the note goes on, the author appears to abandon any attempts to disguise his or her penmanship," the Rocky Mountain News reported.

No appointment had been made for officials to interview the girl's parents, John and Patricia Ramsey, who have hired lawyers and a Washington, D.C., public relations expert. Both parents -- he is a prominent business executive and she a former Miss West Virginia -- have denied involvement in the murder.

The blond, blue-eyed JonBenet was strangled. According to news reports her skull was fractured and she was sexually assaulted. She had been crowned Little Miss Colorado and participated in other beauty contests.

Aaholm also would not confirm a report on KUSA-TV that police searching a second Ramsey home in Michigan were looking for tapes from answering machines and caller identification devices and evidence of threats to the family.

A spokesman for Lockheed Martin said he had no knowledge of any threats against Access Graphics, the Lockheed subsidiary headed by John Ramsey. "Our policy is that we're not making any comment," Ron Meder said.
Boulder-based Access Graphics distributes computer hardware and, in addition to offices throughout the United States, has offices in Canada, Mexico and 17 European countries, Meder said.
